bajkaj-landfill-land-taken-before-paymen.whole: The Integrated Coastal Zone Management and Clean-up Project drew US$14.7 million of a US$17.5 million IDA credit by closing in March 2015. By the Bank's own count it built a sanitary landfill at Bajkaj with 365,000 cubic metres of total capacity, taking 25,000 cubic metres of waste a year, a new 180-metre berth and passenger terminal at Saranda, 2.1 km of rehabilitated sewer line and a 12.9 km replaced trunk main there, and encapsulation of more than 45,000 cubic metres of hazardous waste at Porto Romano. It also records nine village road or square schemes and five water schemes in ten villages including Bajkaj and Palavli, and 27 houses helped under a roof-and-facades programme against a target of up to 62, which it calls 47 per cent of target; no independent count was found. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records that the Executive Directors authorised an Inspection Panel investigation on 1 November 2007 into the demolition of 15 buildings at Jale, and that IDA disbursements were suspended from January 2009 until June 2010.
bajkaj-landfill-land-taken-before-paymen.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (April 2016) results framework and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (February 2017), including project cost, financing and Inspection Panel history.

shkodra-lezha-school-sites-land-cleared.whole: The Education Excellence and Equity Project pooled US$15 million each from IDA, the Council of Europe Development Bank and the European Investment Bank with US$30 million planned from the Albanian government, and spent US$65.9 million, 88 per cent of the US$75 million appraisal estimate. By the Bank's count 22 schools comprising 518 classrooms were built or rehabilitated against a target of 30 schools, six of them new basic schools and four new secondary schools, while the construction component spent 159 per cent of its estimate and the teaching and learning component 14 per cent. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group reports that the completion report's own unit-cost comparison found the project's schools "substantially more expensive" than those of other education projects and, from field visits and the Council of Europe Development Bank's comments, "of poor quality", and that 12 per cent of teachers took part in continuous professional development against a 70 per cent target. Both sets of figures are the Bank's own.
shkodra-lezha-school-sites-land-cleared.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (March 2014) results framework and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (September 2014) on cost, financing, outputs and efficiency.

rn34-colonia-santa-rosa-canteen-eviction.whole: The second National Highway Asset Management loan put US$400 million of Bank money, fully disbursed, into a programme to which the Argentine government contributed US$952.7 million against an appraisal estimate of US$935.1 million. By the Bank's count, rehabilitation and maintenance contracts covering 9,045 km of national road were signed by closing in September 2013, 94 per cent of the 9,608 km planned; average road roughness was held between 3.1 and 3.3 on the International Roughness Index against a target of below 3.5; the maintenance backlog fell from 9.1 per cent in 2006 to about 5 per cent in 2012; and the economic rate of return was recalculated at 41 per cent against 47 per cent at appraisal. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records that only 7 of 13 planned bridges were under restoration at closing, and that of 15 accident black spots 6 had reached bidding and 3 were built. One of the planned road safety corridors had bidding documents ready but untendered; all of these figures are the Bank's own.
rn34-colonia-santa-rosa-canteen-eviction.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (March 2014) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (November 2014) on outputs, road condition, rate of return and the road safety component.

balakhani-landfill-families-and-waste-pi.whole: The Absheron Rehabilitation Program II solid waste project grew from a US$29.5 million IBRD loan to US$76.6 million, all drawn by closing in August 2018, with US$54.28 million of it spent on the Balakhani landfill. By the Bank's count the dump was rebuilt as a sanitary landfill with a 20-year life and 9.7 million tonnes of capacity, with leachate and gas systems running; 6,345 bins were placed in five outer districts of Baku against a revised target of 6,000; and 2,774,416 people were receiving regular collection, with 68 per cent satisfied in a survey against a 70 per cent target. A rate of return of 20 per cent was calculated only at closing, no economic analysis having been done at appraisal. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group reported in 2021 that of 132 informal dumps covering 199 hectares closed over the project period the project itself closed 40 covering 143 hectares and the government the rest, that an estimated 50 per cent of collected waste was still dumped informally, that the state company Tamiz Shahar received 643,000 tonnes in 2017 out of an estimated 1.2 to 1.3 million tonnes collected in Greater Baku, and that electricity sales covered 19 per cent of the waste-to-energy plant's operating costs in 2015-17.
balakhani-landfill-families-and-waste-pi.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (February 2019), the Independent Evaluation Group's review (May 2019) and its 2021 Project Performance Assessment Report, on cost, landfill capacity, collection coverage and the operating company's throughput.

burundi-fibre-backbone-unpaid-compensati.whole: Burundi's fibre backbone was built under the first phase of the Regional Communications Infrastructure Program, a three-country operation with Kenya and Madagascar whose IDA commitment rose to US$226.6 million, of which US$222.4 million was disbursed by closing in December 2016. By the Bank's count the Burundi Backbone System consortium was formed with five major operators and laid fibre optic cable, given as 1,245 km in one part of the Independent Evaluation Group's review and 1,254 km in another. It records eight operators using the landing station against a revised target of six, broadband reaching 34 communes against a target of 20, the price of a full international E1 link falling to US$300 a month, mobile call charges falling from 320 to 60 Burundian francs a minute, the resale price of a 256 kb connection falling from US$2,500 to US$300 a month, and 3,061,706 people, half the population, counted as beneficiaries. No independent verification of these figures was found.
burundi-fibre-backbone-unpaid-compensati.searched: Cached Independent Evaluation Group review (January 2018) of the completion report, which carries the Burundi, Kenya and Madagascar output and outcome figures; no completion report text was cached for this project.

takon-landfill-land-taken-porto-novo.whole: The Second Decentralized City Management Project in Benin cost US$76.17 million by closing in June 2012 against an appraisal estimate of US$37.6 million, made up of US$36.86 million from the original IDA credit, US$37.40 million from additional financing and US$1.9 million from the government. By the Bank's count it delivered 37.63 km of paved road against a revised target of 32.18 km, 15.41 km of primary drainage, 21 latrine blocks, 14 water kiosks, two markets, five new and nine rehabilitated refuse transfer stations, and the Takon landfill itself, which was not operating at closing because the operator's contract was signed six months after the closing date. In Porto-Novo the share of waste collected and carried out of the city is reported rising from 25 per cent in 2004 to 71 per cent in 2012 against a 65 per cent target, with 115,000 more people counted as having improved collection. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records that the solid waste component had a negative net present value of US$4.2 million and a modified return of minus 20 per cent, against 56 per cent for the project as a whole excluding roads, and that the benefits of that component came from a survey of beneficiaries' perceptions without its being clear how the perceptions were quantified.
takon-landfill-land-taken-porto-novo.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2012) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (September 2013), on cost, outputs, Porto-Novo collection rates and the economic analysis of the waste component.

tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.whole: The West Africa Transport and Transit Facilitation Project covered Ghana, Burkina Faso and Mali on IDA credits of US$190 million, of which US$175.6 million was disbursed by closing in June 2015. By the Bank's count 311 km of corridor road was rehabilitated, 54 km in Burkina Faso, 103 km in Ghana and 154 km in Mali; container transit time from Tema port to Burkina Faso fell from seven days to about five and a half and to Bamako from 15 days to about five and a half; truck dwell time at Tema port fell from 48 to 24 hours; and the recalculated rate of return was 12 per cent for Burkina Faso, 13 per cent for Ghana and 14 per cent for Mali, against 21, 15 and 31 per cent at appraisal. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group, which visited Burkina Faso and Ghana in December 2017, reported that Bank financing covered 19 per cent of the corridor, that transit time from Tema to Ouagadougou had since risen to more than seven days because two bridges were being rehabilitated, that the rest stops in Ghana were unfinished and the one built in Mali was not operating, and that a harmonised cargo tracking system was still not running, with only the 825 km Ghanaian section of the 1,900 km corridor operational. It also reported that fixed customs checkpoints in Mali rose from four to six against a target of one.
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2015), the Independent Evaluation Group's review (June 2016) and its 2018 Project Performance Assessment Report based on a December 2017 field visit.

dangriga-market-vendors-income-loss.whole: The Belize Municipal Development Project disbursed US$14.89 million of a US$15 million IBRD loan by closing in November 2016, in a project costing US$15.62 million against an appraisal estimate of US$15.73 million. At Dangriga the Bank's completion report records 7,900 square feet of market rehabilitated and extended, matching the plan, and 1,165 metres of streets and drains rehabilitated against 865 metres planned. Across the nine municipalities it counts 157,233 people, 35,280 of them women, gaining access to improved municipal infrastructure against a revised target of 148,943, along with 33.7 km of drainage and 14.85 km of non-rural road, and reports the nine councils' own-source annual revenues rising 48.1 per cent from an average of about US$11.4 million in the three fiscal years to 2011/12 to about US$16.9 million in the three that followed, from which it calculates a 51.3 per cent rate of return on the capacity-building component. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group calls the evidence that the project-financed training produced that improvement only “circumstantial”; all the figures are the Bank's own.
dangriga-market-vendors-income-loss.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (June 2017), including its Dangriga output table, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (September 2017) on beneficiaries, revenue and the rate of return.

el-alto-avenue-land-paid-for-afterwards.whole: The Bolivia Urban Infrastructure Project began with a US$30 million IDA credit in 2006, added US$24 million, and disbursed US$46.2 million by closing in September 2017. For El Alto the Bank's completion report records 13.44 km of busy main routes improved against a target of 11.16 km and 18,937 metres of sidewalk border built against 12,978 metres planned, with estimated travel time to work falling from 60 to 43 minutes and 197,073 people counted as direct beneficiaries. In the La Paz neighbourhood upgrading part, new sewer connections rose from 5,010 houses to 5,548 against a target of 6,045, and 110,409 people were given all-weather road access within 500 metres against a target of 151,078. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records that US$4.04 million of the El Alto component was cancelled and a US$3.4 million contract in it declared misprocurement, and that the reported rise in neighbourhood property values rests on different measurement methods at appraisal and at closing; all figures are the Bank's own.
el-alto-avenue-land-paid-for-afterwards.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (March 2018) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (September 2018), on cost, cancellation and misprocurement, El Alto road and sidewalk outputs and travel times.

ceara-sanear-ii-resettlement.whole: The Ceará Inclusive Growth loan was a US$240 million IBRD operation paying out against agreed results rather than invoices, of which US$238.75 million was disbursed by closing in June 2012. The Bank's completion report records urban water connections rising from 51,300 in 2007 to 315,800 in 2011 and sewer connections from 22,400 to 139,800, water losses at 26.03 per cent against a 27 per cent target, the state's current fiscal balance rising from R$1,296 million to R$1,882 million, and second-grade literacy rising from 56.0 to 81.4 per cent of students tested between 2009 and 2011. One health target, hospital accreditation by Brazil's National Accreditation Body, was not met and US$1,077,620 of the loan tied to it was cancelled. Those delivery figures are the Bank's and the state government's own and no independent check of them was found; separately, Instituto Trata Brasil, using the federal SNIS data for 2020, reports 60.1 per cent of Ceará's residents with a piped water connection and 29.4 per cent with a sewer connection.
ceara-sanear-ii-resettlement.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2012) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (May 2013), on disbursement-linked indicators, water and sewer connections, fiscal balance and the cancelled tranche. Then Instituto Trata Brasil's 2022 Ceará fact sheet, drawn from the federal SNIS data for 2020, for a coverage figure from outside the project; the Ceará state comptroller's audit of the water company's 2012 accounts could not be opened (robots disallowed).

santos-vila-gilda-stilt-house-resettleme.whole: The Santos municipal project was appraised at US$88 million with a US$44 million IBRD loan, and actual project cost was US$62.37 million. How much of the loan was used is given differently in the Bank's own papers: the text of the Independent Evaluation Group's review gives US$22.77 million disbursed and US$21.23 million cancelled in August 2016, its data sheet gives US$24.12 million, and the completion report's financing table gives US$23.42 million. By the Bank's count 800 households in the Northwest Zone received the full package of municipal services against a target of 2,400, of which 712 families were resettled into new building complexes and 88 had water and housing conditions improved, and 2,950 families were recorded as moved out of flood-prone areas against a target of 45,000. Less than 10 per cent of the planned macro-drainage works and two of 28 planned landslide works were built, which the review puts down to poor engineering designs, procurement issues and implementation problems, while a satisfaction survey of resettled residents reported 95 per cent at Caneleira IV and 94 per cent at Pelé Village II calling the new housing better or much better, against 64 per cent at Quadras 1 and 35; the rate of return, 20.8 per cent at appraisal, was recalculated at closing as a loss of R$92.7 million with a benefit-cost ratio of 0.16.
santos-vila-gilda-stilt-house-resettleme.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (June 2016) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (May 2017), on disbursement and cancellation, resettlement and drainage outputs, the satisfaction survey and the ex-post economic analysis.

thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.whole: Bhutan Urban Development Project II rose from a US$12.0 million IDA credit to US$29.4 million and disbursed US$24.7 million by closing in June 2019. In the Dechencholing, Lanjopakha and Taba local area plans the Bank's completion report records 624 serviced building plots against a target of 300, 14.58 km of roadside footpaths against 10.98 km, 20.40 km of internal roads and 10.39 km of roadside drains as targeted, 20.30 km of water pipeline against a revised 20.70 km and 13.75 km of sewer pipeline against 13.05 km. It counts 732 households newly connected to piped water and 510 to sewers, which its own annex tables put at 86 per cent and 54 per cent of the targets set for the three plans, 364 new building permits at 85 per cent of target, and property taxes collected in Thimphu passing 250 million ngultrum against a target of 200 million for 2011-17. A beneficiary survey commissioned for the project in November 2019 reported 87 per cent of respondents satisfied with piped water and 92 per cent with flush toilets; all of these figures come from the Bank's own reporting.
thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2019) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (March 2020), on plots, pipelines, connections, building permits, property tax and the beneficiary survey.

morupule-b-family-moved-fatal-accidents.whole: Morupule B was a 600 megawatt coal-fired station in a project that cost about US$1,299 million against an appraisal estimate of US$1,662 million, with a Bank loan of US$136.4 million of which US$66.1 million was used. The Bank's completion report says the station was handed to the Botswana Power Corporation in May 2014 “but with significant defects”, naming the boilers and parts of the balance of plant; it was designed for a capacity factor of about 80 per cent and some 4,200 gigawatt-hours a year and was running at a capacity factor closer to 50 per cent because of forced outages, so Botswana went on importing power and running diesel plants. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records the power corporation's government revenue grant rising from US$40 million (455 million pula) in 2011 to US$132 million (1,488 million pula) in 2014, subsidies reaching 66 per cent of its revenues in financial year 2014 when the average tariff covered about 63 per cent of costs, its long-term debt rising from 119 million pula in 2009 to 6,331 million pula in 2014, and the rate of return recalculated at 10.5 per cent against 14.1 per cent at appraisal, or 5.1 per cent with carbon costed at US$30 a ton. Statistics Botswana, the national statistics office, separately reported that locally generated electricity supplied 87.8 per cent of distributed power in the third quarter of 2017, 893,831 megawatt-hours, against 66.5 per cent and 661,245 megawatt-hours a year earlier, with imports falling from 333,355 to 124,612 megawatt-hours.
morupule-b-family-moved-fatal-accidents.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (October 2016) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (January 2017), on plant defects, capacity factor, Botswana Power Corporation subsidies, tariffs, debt and rates of return. Then Statistics Botswana's quarterly electricity generation and distribution brief for the third quarter of 2017 for an independent figure on domestic generation and imports.

chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.whole: The Ningbo New Countryside Development Project fully disbursed a US$50 million IBRD loan in a project costing US$170.33 million by closing in March 2016 against an appraisal estimate of US$157.09 million, with the Chunhu town component costing US$103.36 million against an appraisal estimate of US$78.49 million. By the Bank's count the 6.2 km access road between Fenghua City and Chunhu Town was built, cutting the distance from 24 km to 14.2 km and the journey from 40 minutes to 15, with 13,933 car-equivalent vehicles a day recorded using it against a target of 13,000. The same component delivered 19 km of sewers and a wastewater plant designed for 10,000 cubic metres a day which stood idle for more than a year while the collection network was finished and was treating 6,000 cubic metres a day at closing, 15 km of water transmission mains and a 13 km distribution network, and 76,500 people in 25,500 households in Chunhu recorded as receiving water meeting national standards; the share of Chunhu's wastewater treated reached 84 per cent against a 70 per cent target. Across the project 144 villages completed wastewater works against a target of 150 and 45,500 households received rural wastewater services against a target of 41,000; the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group notes that several of these indicators had no baseline.
chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (October 2016) for the Ningbo New Countryside Development Project and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (February 2017), on component costs, the Fenghua-Chunhu road, water and wastewater outputs and missing baselines.

ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.whole: The Xinjiang Turpan Water Conservation Project fully disbursed a US$100 million IBRD loan in a project costing US$207.85 million by closing in March 2017, against an appraisal estimate of US$204.07 million. The Ertanggou reservoir, with 25 million cubic metres of storage, was one of three dams built, alongside Alagou and Meiyaogou. By the Bank's count 260,000 people gained flood protection, recorded economic losses from flooding fell from 15.48 million yuan in 2009 to zero in 2017, groundwater overdraft was cut by 17.38 million cubic metres in the project irrigation areas against a target of 3.75 million and by 169 million cubic metres across the basin against a target of 37.4 million, 43 water user associations were operating with 21,021 members trained against a target of 2,650, and a financial analysis put farmers' incomes 16 to 20 per cent higher. The rate of return was given as 29 per cent at closing against 21 per cent at appraisal; no independent check of any of these figures was found.
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (October 2017) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (November 2017), on reservoir capacities, flood protection, groundwater, water user associations and rates of return.

lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.whole: The Gansu Cultural and Natural Heritage Protection and Development Project disbursed US$35.02 million of a US$38.40 million IBRD loan across nine sites by closing in June 2015. At the Lutusi Ancient Government Center the Bank's completion report records roads upgraded in the surrounding township, a 418 square metre tourist service centre with a web-based information system, 4,596 square metres of ground surface stabilised and 442 metres of fencing. Its output table lists a planned 85 square metre public toilet, a garbage transfer station and a wastewater plant as dropped for shortage of funds, while its sanitation table records a Lutusi wastewater plant running at its design capacity of 300 cubic metres a day and meeting effluent standards. Visitors to Lutusi are recorded rising from 10,000 in 2008 to 29,000 in 2014 and direct tourism revenue from 0.8 million to 2.5 million yuan, the smallest of the nine sites, where total visitors rose from 2.20 million to 6.97 million and revenue from RMB 1.22 billion to RMB 4.79 billion; all the figures are the Bank's own.
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (February 2016), including its Lutusi output, sanitation, visitor and revenue tables, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (January 2019).

shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.whole: The Jiangxi Shihutang Navigation and Hydropower Complex cost US$344 million against an appraisal estimate of US$319 million, including a US$100 million Bank loan, and closed on schedule in June 2014. It included a 120 megawatt powerhouse designed for 527 million kilowatt-hours a year, a ship lock, 43 km of dikes, 45 km of diversion canals and eight pumping stations, and by the Bank's count protected 4,389 hectares of crop land against a ten-year flood and raised navigable time for 1,000-tonne vessels on the upgraded 38 km channel from 27 to 95 per cent of the year. Output reached 284 gigawatt-hours at closing, 60 per cent of the 472 gigawatt-hour target for 2013, which the completion report attributes to generator installation delays after floods, and cargo through the ship lock in the October to December low-water season was 9,000 tonnes, under 1 per cent of the 1.03 million tonne target, because navigation was suspended until May 2014 during work on the Xiajiang lock 90 km downstream. The rate of return was recalculated at 12.9 per cent against 14.9 per cent at appraisal, and the dam crest access road is reported to have cut the distance between Wanhe Town and Taihe County by about 12 km for some 50,000 users; these are the Bank's figures.
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2014) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (April 2015), on cost, generating capacity and output, ship lock traffic, flood protection and rates of return.

abidjan-lagos-corridor-road-works-deaths.whole: The Abidjan-Lagos Trade and Transport Facilitation Project in Côte d'Ivoire disbursed US$80.4 million of a US$90 million IDA grant by closing in March 2019. By the Bank's count 113.59 km of the Grand-Bassam-Aboisso-Noé road was rehabilitated against a target of 130.3 km, along with transit and parking areas at Noé and Aboisso, the Aboisso and Noé bridges, a footbridge at Aboisso, the Vridi freight terminal and about nine km of access roads, while the rehabilitated market at Elubo was not in use at closing. Roads on the Ivorian section recorded as in good or fair condition rose from 71 per cent in September 2012 to 92 per cent in March 2019, the journey from Abidjan to Noé fell from up to five hours to two, and checkpoints on the 170 km from Noé to Abidjan were counted at four in 2018; border crossing time from Elubo to Noé fell from 37 hours to 14, but the completion report records it back at 47 hours a year after closing in the Noé-to-Elubo direction. The project counted 53 million people living near the corridor as beneficiaries, 33 per cent of them women against a 55 per cent target, and put the rate of return at 20 per cent against 17 per cent on a recalculated appraisal baseline; all the figures come from the Bank's own documents.
abidjan-lagos-corridor-road-works-deaths.searched: Cached World Bank completion report (December 2019) and the Independent Evaluation Group's review (June 2020), on disbursement, kilometres rehabilitated, road condition, travel and border times, beneficiaries and rate of return.

pinheiros-station-collapse-sao-paulo.whole: São Paulo Metro Line 4 Phase 1 cost US$1,776.3 million against an appraisal estimate of US$933.9 million, with US$304.0 million drawn from an IBRD loan, US$304.1 million from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, US$922.0 million from the State of São Paulo and an estimated US$246.1 million from the private concession. The six Phase 1 stations opened between 25 May 2010 and 15 September 2011, with bus integration at all six, and the Bank’s completion report records the line carrying over 600,000 passengers a day after six months in operation; the Independent Evaluation Group adds that the Bank’s own task team put daily ridership at close to 700,000 in October 2012. By the Bank’s count the metro’s share of motorised trips in the metropolitan region rose from 16 per cent in 2001 to 19.3 per cent against a revised target of 17.5 per cent, and the generalised cost of travel between Vila Sonia and Luz fell from 104 minutes to 73 against a revised target of 82. The rate of return was recalculated at 13.8 per cent against 17.7 per cent at appraisal, with net present value of US$364 million against US$554 million; these are the lender’s own figures and those of the state metro company that built the line, and no independent audit of them was found.
pinheiros-station-collapse-sao-paulo.searched: Recovered the 2012 completion report and the 2013 Independent Evaluation Group review from the Bank's document API and read them in text form; took cost and financing from Annex 1, station opening dates and ridership from the completion report, mode share and travel cost from the results framework, and rates of return from Annex 3 and the review.
